coverage_rule: Two individually named characters and one direct co-investigation relation supported by Seven Seas' official volume-one synopsis only. No named identity is inferred for the aggrieved young man, and no unsupported clan, sect, cultivation-system, artifact, ghost/corpse, place, adaptation, or later-volume information is asserted.
omissions: The unnamed aggrieved young man whose body Wei Wuxian awakens in, because this witness does not name him.
All other characters, clans, sects, titles, places, artifacts, ghosts/corpses, and plot material outside the publisher synopsis.
Chinese-serialization specifics, including Hanzi character-name forms and any web-serial chapter or revision details, because no Chinese witness is included in this pass.
Donghua, manhua, audio-drama, live-action, game, unofficial-translation, and later licensed-volume continuities.
uncertainties: This is a narrow licensed publisher-metadata pass rather than a page-by-page reading of the English volume or a primary Chinese text pass.
The witness gives pinyin-form names (Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji) but does not print Hanzi; Hanzi aliases are therefore intentionally not supplied from external sources.

The publisher markets the novel as danmei/Boys' Love and describes two men finding one another across life and death, but this synopsis alone does not warrant a more specific relationship-status claim.
No censorship claim is made: adaptation differences and any censorship context require separate, adaptation-specific evidence.
The synopsis contains war, death, fear/stigmatization, a soul sacrifice, revenge, and a second-life identity premise; broader content warnings and spoilers require the full volume.
evidence_basis: Seven Seas' official volume-one record identifies the licensed edition, translation credits, danmei/Boys' Love marketing category, Wei Wuxian, Lan Wangji, demonic cultivation, Wei's death, and his awakening in another young man's body. It is the sole basis for character-level claims.
